extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal benchmark for evaluating college-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across 30 subjects and 6 disciplines using 11.5K questions from exams, quizzes, and textbooks.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated in three stages: selecting subjects where visual inputs are common, recruiting over 50 university students specializing in those majors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when necessary, and then performing duplicate removal, format/typo checking, and difficulty filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed by authors and removed; problems were standardized for format and typos; authors assigned difficulty levels and excluded about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection and removal, format standardization, typo correction, and exclusion of very easy questions that did not meet benchmark design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students specializing in the selected majors collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and created new questions when necessary. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright and license regulations and to avoid questions with immediately available answers to reduce contamination.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors reviewed suspected duplicates, checked formatting and typos, categorized problems into four difficulty levels, and excluded around 10% of very easy items. The paper also reports that annotation errors accounted for 2% of 150 analyzed GPT-4V error cases.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors; 50 college students from various disciplines and subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A version change log is included in the supplementary material, and the leaderboard is live-updating.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age and gender appear in some questions; the benchmark also covers disciplines including Health & Medicine and Public Health.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is motivated by monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled adult labor, creating risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may carry manual curation biases, focuses on college-level subjects, and is not sufficient by itself for testing Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults and college exams are not the only relevant tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of multimodal models for zero-shot, few-shot, validation, and test settings; the dataset is split into a few-shot development set, a validation set for hyperparameter selection, and a test set.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: MMMU, like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57]... We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMMU, constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions... Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting to assess the capability of models to generate accurate answers without fine-tuning or few-shot demonstrations on our benchmark. We also report the few-shot results of some selected models in the Appendix.
